content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue installing [product_name] on Ubuntu 17.10. Although JAVA is already on my system, the installer still tries to add it, and I haven't found a way to set up [product_name] without JAVA. If anyone has advice or suggestions, I'd appreciate it. Thank you.
I have found a workaround. Since JRE was already installed, I was able to run [product_name] directly from the /Linux/Application_64 directory without further installation. [url]

analysis.insight_summary: The user had difficulties installing [product_name] on Ubuntu 17.10, noticing that the installer requested JAVA installation even though JAVA (JRE) was present. There were no clear alternatives or instructions, causing confusion. Ultimately, the user managed to run the software directly from its folder, which bypassed the installer requirement.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the installer to detect existing JAVA installations and allow for a more straightforward setup of [product_name] on Linux.
